cards.method: Gravity models of bilateral trade (OLS / PPML / importer-exporter fixed effects / Bonus vetus OLS / Head-Mayer-Ries tetrads)
cards.when: a bilateral (dyadic) trade panel/cross-section {origin, destination, flow, distance, (GDPs), (dummies)} and you want to estimate the elasticity of trade with respect to distance/income/trade-cost proxies -> choose the estimator according to how you handle the Multilateral Resistance (MR) terms and the zero flows
cards.when_not: a univariate time series with no dyadic structure; input-output or network work (-> #48-#55); a plain panel OLS or fixed-effects fit with no gravity structure (-> #46/#47); censored or tobit trade (separate cards); data ingestion (a file upload — a frontend route, not a node)

alternatives.criterion: the flow contains ZEROS and/or heteroskedasticity; you want consistent estimates in the multiplicative form (the log-of-gravity critique) — the default-safe estimator; supply the incomes ALREADY logged as additional_regressors
you want the traditional log-log gravity with explicit income regressors; ONLY if flow>0 everywhere (no zeros) and you do not care about the MR bias (Anderson-van Wincoop) — a baseline/comparison

you want to absorb ALL the monadic/MR terms with country dummies (theoretically consistent in a cross-section); the unilateral GDPs are no longer estimated — for a clean estimate of dyadic trade-cost elasticities
you want MR-consistent estimates WITH comparative statics preserved (a first-order log-linear Taylor MR approximation through simple averages) — when you need counterfactuals that FE do not allow

you want to eliminate the monadic effects without dummies, through a reference exporter and importer (a ratio of ratios); it needs at least one dyadic regressor; multiway=True gives multi-way clustered standard errors (Cameron, Gelbach & Miller 2011)

output_key_fields: coefficients: a long-format frame {term, estimate, std_error, statistic, p_value} (the robust route leaves the p-value blank; the multi-way clustered test returns four columns including it)
distance_term / distance_coef: the name and value of the elasticity with respect to (logged) distance — the central gravity result

fitstats: a named record {n_obs, r_squared, adj_r_squared, sigma, log_lik, aic, bic, deviance, null_deviance, pseudo_r2, df_residual}, blank where undefined; pseudo_r2 = 1 - deviance/null deviance, and only for the GLM and PPML routes
method / fit_class / robust + method-specific flags (family, accepts_zeros, uie, mr_terms, fixed_effects, method_family, multiway, filter_origin, filter_destination)
fit: the raw fitted object (glm/lm/rlm/coeftest; to_mcp -> a stub)
interpretation_traps: distance & (for OLS/FE/BVU/tetrads) the dependent variable and the incomes are logged AUTOMATICALLY -> they must be STRICTLY POSITIVE; non-positive values are dropped SILENTLY (log=NaN/-Inf, verified: gravity_zeros 500->355 observations with no warning) -> hard gates; for zero flows use gr_ppml (>=0)

gr_ols with uie=True (unitary income elasticities) is BROKEN upstream: the formula refers to log-income columns that the unitary path never creates, so it fails with 'object not found' (verified live) -> HARD-GATED; the only working value is uie=False, with explicit income regressors
robust=True selects the M-estimator, whose summary gives three columns (value, standard error, t) with NO p-value -> the p_value stays blank in coefficients (expected, not an error)

gr_tetrads requires at least one additional dyadic regressor (a trade agreement, contiguity); leaving it unset gives a cryptic join error (verified) -> a gate; filter_origin and filter_destination must EXIST as codes in the code columns
gr_ppml: a quasi-Poisson family with a log link leaves AIC and the log-likelihood blank, since it is a quasi-likelihood; use pseudo_r2, not r_squared

gr_fixed_effects: the unilateral GDPs are absorbed by the country FE and are NOT estimated -> do not ask for them as coefficients; only the dyadic terms (distance + additional_regressors) are interpretable
the estimators are DETERMINISTIC given the data (least squares, IRLS, the M-estimator, the clustered covariance) -> NO seed is needed; two runs were confirmed identical
sources: Wölwer, Burgard & Kunst — the PPML, OLS, fixed-effects, BVU and tetrads estimators, with their references
Silva JMCS & Tenreyro S (2006) 'The Log of Gravity' Review of Economics and Statistics 88(4) 641-658 doi:10.1162/rest.88.4.641 (PPML)
Feenstra RC (2002) 'Border effects and the gravity equation: consistent methods for estimation' Scottish Journal of Political Economy 49(5) 491-506 (fixed effects)

Baier SL & Bergstrand JH (2009) 'Bonus vetus OLS: a simple method for approximating international trade-cost effects using the gravity equation' Journal of International Economics 77(1) 77-85 doi:10.1016/j.jinteco.2008.10.004; Baier & Bergstrand (2010) Cambridge University Press ch.4 (BVU)
Head K, Mayer T & Ries J (2010) 'The erosion of colonial trade linkages after independence' Journal of International Economics 81(1) 1-14 doi:10.1016/j.jinteco.2010.01.002 (tetrads)

Head K & Mayer T (2014) 'Gravity Equations: Workhorse, Toolkit, and Cookbook' Handbook of International Economics vol 4, 131-195 (a survey); Anderson JE & van Wincoop E (2003) 'Gravity with Gravitas' (the MR terms)

cards.method: Penalized Poisson PML gravity with high-dimensional fixed effects (an HDFE PPML baseline; a single-lambda lasso/ridge/plugin; a lasso/ridge path + a BIC-selected lambda)
cards.when: structural gravity on ONE long bilateral-trade panel (exporter x importer x [time]): PPML estimation with several HDFE (exporter-time, importer-time, pair) and MANY dummy regressors (e.g. trade-agreement provisions) -> baseline coefficients (pp_hdfe); penalized selection of a relevant subset (pp_penalized_hdfe at a single lambda; pp_ml_fit over a path + BIC, or a plugin lasso)
cards.when_not: log-OLS gravity on positive flows only (Santos Silva-Tenreyro: biased under heteroskedasticity/zeros); few regressors with no need for variable selection (use fepois/feglm, #33); economic complexity/ECI-PCI (#237); a non-count/negative dependent variable; time-series gravity without a dyadic panel; data ingestion (a file upload — a frontend route, not a node)

alternatives.criterion: you want the (unpenalized) HDFE PPML gravity baseline: coefficients + robust/cluster SE + deviance/BIC, with no variable selection
you want a penalized fit at ONE known lambda: lasso (L1, it zeroes out/selects) or ridge (L2, shrinkage without zeroing)
you want a plugin lasso with data-driven coefficient-specific penalty loadings (Breinlich et al. 2021); it REQUIRES a cluster
you want the WHOLE penalization path over a vector of lambdas and automatic selection of the lambda that MINIMISES the BIC (+ optional post-lasso de-biasing)
you want the plugin lasso through the path API (it ignores lambdas and returns the plugin-selected fit); it REQUIRES a cluster

output_key_fields: pp_hdfe: coefficients (named per regressor) + se + deviance + bic + n_obs/n_coef + fixed_effects (the labels) + penalty='none'
pp_penalized_hdfe: coefficients (named) + deviance + bic + lambda + penalty + plugin + n_selected, the non-zero ones, + phi, the plugin penalty loadings, where they apply

pp_ml_fit: beta_path (a regressors-by-lambdas matrix, with row labels) + lambdas + bic_path (a lambda-and-BIC matrix) + selected_lambda + selected_bic + selected_coefficients, the column at the minimum BIC, + n_selected + deviance (blank along the path) + phi for the plugin route + seed
interpretation_traps: PPML models E[y]=exp(x*beta) in LEVELS rather than logs, so it handles zero flows and heteroskedasticity; the dependent variable MUST be non-negative, since a negative or missing value gives NaN and then a cryptic crash — blocked by a gate

the fixed effects MUST arrive as a LIST (a list of names means an interaction effect); the wrapper normalises that, converting a plain vector of names into a list — otherwise the routine fails cryptically
the lasso zeroes coefficients out (n_selected = the number of non-zero ones); ridge NEVER zeroes any (n_selected is usually all of them)

the information-criterion selection takes the minimum finite BIC along bic_path and is DETERMINISTIC; a degenerate, entirely blank BIC — for instance too large a lambda, giving an all-zero fit — returns the first lambda with a blank BIC
plugin=True, in pp_penalized_hdfe and pp_ml_fit, REQUIRES a cluster for the cluster-robust penalty loadings -> a gate; it returns phi, the per-coefficient loadings
a non-numeric regressor is coerced SILENTLY into a meaningless coefficient -> a hard gate: the regressors must all be numeric, with no gaps

the IRLS and elastic-net routines are deterministic and identical when seeded; the seed is exposed as defence in depth; the raw fit is NOT returned, since its per-observation internals are heavy, so it serialises to a stub; the internal, cross-validation, observation-selection, bootstrap and iceberg helpers were omitted as outside the estimator surface
sources: Santos Silva & Tenreyro 2006 'The Log of Gravity' Review of Economics and Statistics 88(4) 641-658 (the PPML gravity estimator)
Correia, Guimaraes & Zylkin 2020 'Fast Poisson estimation with high-dimensional fixed effects' The Stata Journal 20(1) 95-115 (ppmlhdfe / the fast HDFE PPML backbone)

Breinlich, Corradi, Rocha, Ruta, Santos Silva & Zylkin 2021 'Machine Learning in International Trade Research: Evaluating the Impact of Trade Agreements' World Bank Policy Research WP 9629 (penalized/plugin PPML provision selection)
Belloni, Chernozhukov, Hansen & Kozbur 2016 'Inference in High-Dimensional Panel Models With an Application to Gun Control' JBES 34(4) 590-605 (the plugin lasso penalty loadings)

cards.method: Economic complexity: RCA (the Balassa index), ECI/PCI (fitness/reflections/eigenvalues), product-space proximity
cards.when: a bipartite country×product export panel -> the Revealed Comparative Advantage (Balassa), the Economic/Product Complexity Index (ECI/PCI), and product-space proximity (country×country / product×product similarity) for analysing specialisation, diversification & productive capabilities
cards.when_not: gravity/PPML trade-flow models (#237/#238 in the same category); a time series of one variable (no bipartite structure); input-output/network centrality (#48-55); downstream product-space diffusion (outlook/density/distance/projections — a separate card); data ingestion (a file upload — a frontend route, not a node)

alternatives.alt: ec_balassa (discrete=True gives 0/1 specialization; False a continuous RCA)
alternatives.criterion: you want the country×product Revealed Comparative Advantage matrix + diversification (rowSums) & ubiquity (colSums)
you want the ECI per country + the PCI per product; fitness=non-linear iterative (Tacchella); reflections=iterated averaging (Hidalgo-Hausmann); eigenvalues=the 2nd eigenvector
you want product-space similarity matrices: country×country AND/OR product×product (Hausmann-Hidalgo)

output_key_fields: ec_balassa: balassa_index (a country×product matrix with axis labels; discrete => 0/1) + diversification (named numeric per country, rowSums) + ubiquity (per product, colSums) + n_countries/n_products/discrete/cutoff
ec_complexity: eci (named numeric per country) + pci (named numeric per product) + method/iterations/extremality/discrete/cutoff + countries/products

ec_proximity: proximity_country (a country-by-country matrix, when requested) + proximity_product (a product-by-product matrix, when requested) + compute + n_countries/n_products, blank for a side that was not requested
interpretation_traps: balassa_index silently ACCEPTS negative values & returns a plausible-but-wrong RCA -> a hard non-negativity gate (the Balassa index is defined only on non-negative exports)
a single country OR a single product -> a degenerate all-1 RCA (silently wrong) -> a hard gate requiring >=2 countries AND >=2 products
discrete=True (a 0/1 RCA at or above the cutoff) is the classic input for the complexity indices and the proximities; a continuous RCA changes the meaning of every downstream metric
extremality affects ONLY method='fitness' (it is inert for reflections/eigenvalues but is still passed); eigenvalues prints a cosmetic sign-correction message (suppressMessages, not a warning)
deterministic (linear algebra / iterated reflections); no RNG -> no seed; identical over 2 runs is pinned in the tests
a TERMINAL node: no register/handle chaining; it returns chart-ready numbers (matrices + the ECI/PCI vectors), not a fitted model
sources: Balassa 1965 'Trade Liberalisation and Revealed Comparative Advantage' The Manchester School 33(2) 99-123 (the Balassa/RCA index)
Hidalgo & Hausmann 2009 'The building blocks of economic complexity' PNAS 106(26) 10570-10575 (ECI/PCI, the method of reflections)
Hausmann, Hidalgo et al. 2014 'The Atlas of Economic Complexity' MIT Press (ECI/PCI, the product space, proximity)
Hidalgo, Klinger, Barabasi, Hausmann 2007 'The Product Space Conditions the Development of Nations' Science 317(5837) 482-487 (proximity / the product space)
Tacchella, Cristelli, Caldarelli, Gabrielli, Pietronero 2012 'A New Metrics for Countries Fitness and Products Complexity' Scientific Reports 2:723 (the fitness method)

cards.when: trade policy changes bilateral flows and also relative prices everywhere, and a partial-equilibrium estimate misses the second effect entirely
cards.when_not: you only need the partial elasticity; the required expenditure and production data are unavailable

alternatives.criterion: the direct trade elasticity only
general equilibrium with multilateral resistance
production structure matters

output_key_fields: counterfactual_trade: bilateral flows under the counterfactual
multilateral_resistance: inward and outward terms, before and after
welfare: real income change per country
convergence: whether the equilibrium solved
interpretation_traps: MULTILATERAL RESISTANCE IS THE WHOLE POINT: a bilateral tariff change alters every country's price index, and a partial-equilibrium calculation misses effects that are frequently larger than the direct one
the counterfactual is conditional on the estimated trade elasticity, and welfare results scale directly with it
the equilibrium is solved up to a normalisation; welfare changes are relative to the chosen numeraire
sources: Anderson & van Wincoop 2003 (American Economic Review 93:170-192)
Yotov, Piermartini, Monteiro & Larch 2016, An Advanced Guide to Trade Policy Analysis
Larch & Yotov 2016 (WTO Working Paper ERSD-2016-08)
gegravity

cards.method: Gravity data assembly and estimation workflow
cards.when: assembling the bilateral panel a gravity estimation needs, with the fixed effects and zero flows handled correctly
cards.when_not: the panel is already assembled; the country coverage changes so much that fixed effects are not identified

alternatives.criterion: the modern standard
wrong whenever there are zero flows
you want to model selection into trading

output_key_fields: panel: the assembled bilateral panel
estimates: gravity coefficients
zeros: how many flows are zero, and how they were handled
fixed_effects: the effects absorbed
interpretation_traps: DROPPING ZERO FLOWS BY LOGGING BIASES EVERY COEFFICIENT: zeros are a large share of bilateral pairs and are informative, which is the single strongest argument for PPML
exporter-time and importer-time fixed effects are what control multilateral resistance; omitting them is the classic gold-medal mistake
intra-national trade must be included for many policy questions or the estimates are not comparable to theory
sources: Head & Mayer 2014, Gravity equations: workhorse, toolkit, and cookbook (Handbook of International Economics 4)
Yotov, Piermartini, Monteiro & Larch 2016, An Advanced Guide to Trade Policy Analysis
gme

cards.method: Trade in value added and global value-chain participation
cards.when: gross bilateral trade double-counts intermediates, and value-added measures are what map to income and employment
cards.when_not: the analysis is about gross flows such as tariff revenue; no input-output table covers the countries needed

alternatives.criterion: tariffs and logistics
income and employment implications
position in the supply chain

output_key_fields: value_added_exports: domestic value added embodied in exports
double_counting: the gross-minus-value-added wedge
gvc_participation: backward and forward participation indices
position: upstreamness of each country-sector
interpretation_traps: GROSS EXPORTS DOUBLE-COUNT INTERMEDIATES that cross borders repeatedly; for highly integrated supply chains the gross figure can exceed value added by a large multiple
the decomposition depends entirely on the input-output table used, and different databases disagree materially
backward and forward participation measure different things and a country can be high in one and low in the other
sources: Koopman, Wang & Wei 2014 (American Economic Review 104:459-494)
Borin & Mancini 2019 (World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 8804)
pymrio

cards.method: Trade indices: revealed comparative advantage, Lafay and Grubel-Lloyd
cards.when: summarising a country's specialisation and the nature of its trade, which raw flows cannot show
cards.when_not: the product classification changes over the period; the country's trade is too concentrated for indices to be informative

alternatives.criterion: export specialisation against the world
symmetric and bounded, unlike the raw index
how much trade is intra-industry

output_key_fields: rca: revealed comparative advantage per product
normalised_rca: the symmetric version, bounded in minus one to one
grubel_lloyd: intra-industry trade share
lafay: the contribution-to-trade-balance index
interpretation_traps: THE RAW BALASSA INDEX IS ASYMMETRIC -- bounded below by zero and unbounded above -- so it cannot be averaged or used in a regression without transformation; the normalised version exists for that
the Grubel-Lloyd index rises mechanically with the level of product aggregation, so cross-study comparisons need the same classification level
these indices reflect trade policy and transport costs as much as comparative advantage, despite the name
sources: Balassa 1965 (Manchester School 33:99-123)
Grubel & Lloyd 1975, Intra-Industry Trade
Lafay 1992, The measurement of revealed comparative advantages (International Trade Modelling)

cards.method: PPML with high-dimensional fixed effects and multiway clustering
cards.when: the gravity workhorse: a Poisson estimator that handles zeros, heteroskedasticity and three-way fixed effects at once
cards.when_not: the outcome is not a non-negative flow; the fixed-effect structure leaves no variation in the policy variable

alternatives.criterion: the standard
invalid with zeros and biased under heteroskedasticity
an alternative if the conditional variance is proportional to the square of the mean

output_key_fields: params: coefficients as semi-elasticities
absorbed: fixed effects removed and their level counts
separation: observations dropped by perfect separation
cluster: the clustering applied
interpretation_traps: THE LOG-LINEAR MODEL IS BIASED UNDER HETEROSKEDASTICITY EVEN WITHOUT ZEROS, because the expectation of the log is not the log of the expectation -- this is the Silva-Tenreyro result and it is the reason PPML replaced OLS
perfect separation silently drops observations and whole fixed-effect groups, changing the estimation sample without warning
clustering on pairs is standard because bilateral flows are correlated over time within a pair
sources: Silva & Tenreyro 2006 (Review of Economics and Statistics 88:641-658)
Correia, Guimaraes & Zylkin 2020 (Stata Journal 20:95)
Weidner & Zylkin 2021 (Journal of International Economics 132:103513)
pyfixest
